DECOVERAI · DISCOVERY REFERENCE

Attorney-client privilege definition

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc.

Matter

IRS Examination — Coastal Solar Credit Program

Issued to

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc., Attn: Legal Department, Portland, OR 97209

Issuing agency

Internal Revenue Service, Examination Division

Case no.

EX-2023-04471

Date issued

May 23, 2023

Response due

June 13, 2023 (21 days)

Revenue agent

Kevin Tran

Version

v1.0 — prepared July 16, 2026

I. Applicable matter

This definition applies to the IRS's examination of Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc. ("CTH" or "the Company") in connection with the Coastal Solar Credit Program (the "Program"), a renewable-energy / land-conservation tax credit program administered by Alder Point Partners and, for a period, brokered by Bellhaven Advisory.

"The Program" means the Coastal Solar Credit Program in its entirety, including credit origination, land-parcel eligibility determinations, marketing and broker placement activity, and related investor, banking, and tax records.

Where the subpoena's scope differs from the privilege analysis below, refer to the Responsiveness Definition for scope-specific guidance. Privilege and responsiveness are assessed independently (Section VI).

II. Legal standard

A document is protected by attorney-client privilege when all three of the following elements are satisfied. All three are mandatory — satisfying one or two is not sufficient.

A. Confidential communication

The communication was made with the intention of confidentiality and has been kept private. Sharing it with, or making it in the presence of, anyone outside the privileged circle defined in Section III generally destroys the privilege.

B. Between privileged persons

The communication occurred between CTH (acting through its personnel) and its attorneys, or the attorneys' agents (paralegals, associates, or other agents retained to assist with legal work). Being between privileged persons alone does not establish privilege — the purpose element (Section II.C) must independently be satisfied.

C. For the primary purpose of legal advice

The primary reason for the communication was to seek or provide legal assistance. This is presumed for substantive communications between CTH personnel and its counsel, unless the communication primarily relates to:

— Business, operational, or financial matters (e.g., budget approvals, staffing, scheduling)

— Administrative transmittals with no legal analysis (e.g., "here's the engagement letter," "please sign and return")

— Preservation/compliance directives issued company-wide (e.g., legal hold notices — see Rule V.C)

— Factual reporting that has not yet been analyzed or advised upon by counsel (see Rule V.B)

III. Privileged parties in this matter

In-house counsel: John Ellery, Head of Legal, Cascade Timber Holdings.

Outside counsel: L&L Associates, formally engaged February 24, 2023 [EMAIL-021] to advise on the internal review of the Program following the whistleblower complaint.

— Grace Lin — Partner

— Mia Chen — Associate

— Alan Brooks — Paralegal

Client organization (Cascade Timber Holdings personnel): Elena Marlowe (CEO), Robert Denniston (CFO), Sarah Nguyen (Chief Compliance Officer), Marcus Webb (Board Chair), Frank Delgado (VP Investor Relations), Craig Sato (Controller), Dan Osei (IT Director), Wendy Park (HR Director), and CTH's Board of Directors.

Any attorney above can independently create a privileged communication with any member of the client organization. No single attorney's presence is required to establish privilege — the analysis runs off the roles above, not any one person's name.

IV. Non-privileged third parties

Alder Point Partners and Bellhaven Advisory are separate companies, not part of CTH's privileged circle. Their personnel are not counsel for CTH or for each other in this matter:

— Alder Point Partners: Priya Shah, Tom Reyes, Jay Whitfield (aka "Kane"), Nina Alvarez

— Bellhaven Advisory: Derek Holt, Renee Ford

Their presence on an otherwise-privileged CTH email (e.g., Ellery or L&L Associates on the thread) vitiates privilege for that communication. There is no joint-defense or common-interest agreement between CTH and Alder Point Partners or Bellhaven in this matter — to the contrary, CTH's internal review examines whether Alder Point's and Bellhaven's own conduct exposed CTH to liability, so their interests are not aligned with CTH's for privilege purposes.

GreenAcre Land Survey Co. is an independent third-party vendor; its survey findings are not privileged merely because they were later relied upon in CTH's internal review (see the Work Product Definition, Section III, on fact work product commissioned in anticipation of litigation).

V. Practical rules and worked examples

A. Document markings are a starting signal, not the answer

In this collection, documents carrying an X-Decover-Privileged: Yes header and an in-body privilege banner are reliably privileged — but always confirm against the substance of Section II rather than relying on the marking alone. A marking with no actual legal advice in the body would not be privileged in a real-world review.

B. Factual reporting is not yet legal advice

A report that triggers a later privileged response is not itself privileged if it contains no legal advice.

WORKED EXAMPLE

[EMAIL-019] (Sarah Nguyen to John Ellery and Elena Marlowe, reporting the whistleblower complaint and recommending an internal review) is factual reporting — not privileged. [EMAIL-020], Ellery's response the next day providing legal advice "in anticipation of potential regulatory inquiry," is privileged.

C. Legal hold notices are administrative, not privileged

[EMAIL-024], the company-wide legal hold notice sent by Ellery, is a preservation directive, not a confidential communication seeking or giving legal advice — even though it originates from counsel and concerns the matter under review. Treat legal hold notices the same as engagement letters and invoices (Rule V.D): administrative, not privileged.

D. Engagement letters are administrative; the cover email may not be

The LL_Associates_Engagement_Letter.pdf attachment is an administrative business record describing the terms of retention — not privileged by itself.

WORKED EXAMPLE

Evaluate the cover email independently: [EMAIL-021] (Ellery formally engaging Grace Lin and directing that related communications be treated as privileged) itself reflects a request for legal services and is privileged, even though the attached letter is not. Each family member is assessed on its own content (Rule V.F).

E. Legal strategy discussion is privileged even when it touches budget

WORKED EXAMPLE

[EMAIL-026] (Robert Denniston to Elena Marlowe, questioning L&L's cost estimate) has no attorney on the thread and is not privileged. [EMAIL-027], Ellery's reply — which discusses review approach and a faster review methodology to hit budget and the subpoena deadline — is privileged: an attorney is a participant, and the content reflects legal strategy for structuring the review, not mere administrative budgeting.

F. Document family independence

Each item in a document family (email plus attachments) is evaluated on its own content. A privileged cover email does not automatically make an attachment privileged, and vice versa. Apply this whenever an email attaches a spreadsheet, deck, or PDF — assess the attachment's own content for legal advice independent of the cover email.

G. No attorney involved means no privilege

If no CTH attorney (Ellery) and no L&L Associates attorney or agent participates in a communication — even if the subject matter is the Program or the internal review — the communication cannot be privileged. The topic alone does not create privilege.

VI. The Kovel agent doctrine

A. Legal standard

Under *United States v. Kovel*, 296 F.2d 918 (2d Cir. 1961), attorney-client privilege can extend to communications with a non-lawyer third party who is retained by the attorney (not the client) to help the attorney render legal advice — for example, an accountant retained by counsel to translate financial data into terms the attorney can use to give legal advice. The doctrine does not create a freestanding privilege for the third party; it treats the third party as functionally part of the attorney's team for the limited purpose of facilitating legal advice.

A person or vendor qualifies as a Kovel agent only if all of the following are true:

— Retained by the attorney (or at the attorney's direction), not retained directly by the client for an independent business purpose

— The vendor's role is to help the attorney understand facts or perform tasks necessary to render legal advice, not to provide the client with ordinary business, operational, or compliance services

— The communications at issue are within the scope of that legal-facilitation role, not general business correspondence that happens to pass through the vendor

Do not presume Kovel status from a vendor's mere presence on a Program-related communication. The presumption runs the other way: absent evidence the vendor was engaged by counsel to facilitate legal advice, treat the vendor as an ordinary third party whose presence vitiates privilege under Section IV.

B. Worked example — the two "M2" vendors

This matter involves two same-named vendors that must not be conflated. They are organizationally unrelated and serve opposite roles under the Kovel analysis:

M2 DISCOVERY — A KOVEL AGENT

M2 Discovery is the document-review and technology-assisted-review (TAR) platform retained by L&L Associates to support the internal review of the Program. [EMAIL-027] (Ellery's "faster review approach" discussion with Denniston and Marlowe) reflects L&L Associates' use of M2 Discovery's TAR workflow to meet the review budget and the subpoena deadline. Because M2 Discovery is retained by counsel to facilitate the legal review — not by CTH for an independent business purpose — its personnel's participation in review-strategy communications with L&L Associates does not vitiate privilege, and such communications may independently qualify as work product (see the Work Product Definition, Section IV.C, on vendor work performed at counsel's direction).

M2 COMPLIANCE — NOT A KOVEL AGENT

M2 Compliance is a separate state tax-credit filing and registration vendor retained directly by Alder Point Partners on the business side to prepare and file ongoing state renewable-energy credit certifications. It was not retained by any attorney and does not facilitate legal advice — it performs ordinary business filing work. M2 Compliance's presence on a communication (e.g., a routine state filing status update) does not support a privilege claim even though the subject matter is the Program. If M2 Compliance appears on a thread that also includes Ellery or L&L Associates, apply Section IV: M2 Compliance is a non-Kovel third party, and its presence vitiates ACP for that communication.

The distinguishing question in both cases is the same

Who retained the vendor, and for what purpose? Retained by counsel to facilitate legal advice → Kovel agent, presence does not vitiate privilege. Retained by the client (or by Alder Point Partners) for business, operational, or compliance services → ordinary third party, presence vitiates privilege under Section IV. Do not infer Kovel status from the "M2" name alone — M2 Discovery and M2 Compliance are evaluated independently, and confusing the two is the most common error in applying this rule.

VII. Privilege and responsiveness are independent

A document can be both privileged and responsive to the subpoena (e.g., [EMAIL-012], Ellery's risk-assessment memo, is responsive to Category 1 / tax-credit transactions and privileged — it is logged, not produced). A document can also be responsive but not privileged (e.g., the marketing deck attached to [EMAIL-001]), or privileged but of marginal responsiveness (e.g., internal review strategy discussions unrelated to any of the five subpoena categories). Always assess the two questions separately.

Confidential — Prepared for Legal Review

DECOVERAI · DISCOVERY REFERENCE

Work product doctrine definition

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc.

Matter

IRS Examination — Coastal Solar Credit Program

Issued to

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc., Attn: Legal Department, Portland, OR 97209

Issuing agency

Internal Revenue Service, Examination Division

Case no.

EX-2023-04471

Date issued

May 23, 2023

Response due

June 13, 2023 (21 days)

Revenue agent

Kevin Tran

Version

v1.0 — prepared July 16, 2026

I. Applicable matter

This definition applies to materials prepared by or for Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc. or its representatives in anticipation of litigation or a government proceeding concerning the Coastal Solar Credit Program.

II. Legal standard

The work product doctrine protects documents and tangible things prepared in anticipation of litigation or for trial by or for a party or its representative (including attorneys, consultants, or agents), regardless of whether an attorney authored the material. Unlike attorney-client privilege, work product does not require an attorney to be a participant in the communication — it requires only that the material was prepared because of anticipated litigation or a government proceeding, and not in the ordinary course of business.

Two tiers apply:

— Fact work product — factual investigation/compilation material (lower protection; discoverable on a substantial-need/undue-hardship showing).

— Opinion work product — material reflecting the mental impressions, legal theories, or strategy of counsel (near-absolute protection).

III. Anticipation-of-litigation trigger date

Materials created before the trigger date below are ordinary-course business records, even if they later become important evidence. Materials created at or after the trigger date, because of the anticipated proceeding, are work product candidates.

TRIGGER DATE — FEBRUARY 24, 2023

[EMAIL-021], CTH's formal engagement of L&L Associates to advise on an internal review of the Program, "given the complaint received last week" (referencing the whistleblower complaint received February 20, 2023, [EMAIL-019]). This is the bright-line date after which internal-review materials are prepared in anticipation of litigation/regulatory action. Reinforced by [EMAIL-023] (IRS subpoena received, May 23, 2023) and [EMAIL-024] (legal hold notice, June 13, 2023).

Documents predating February 24, 2023 — e.g., [EMAIL-003]/[EMAIL-015]/[EMAIL-016] (original parcel eligibility concerns), the underlying Land_Parcel_Data_Northwest.csv, and the GreenAcre survey commissioned to investigate the acreage discrepancy — are ordinary business records, not work product, even though they became central evidence in the later review. They may still be responsive (Category 1) and, separately, some may be privileged if they reflect legal advice — analyze independently.

IV. Worked examples

A. Interim findings memo — opinion work product (and privileged)

WORKED EXAMPLE

Privileged_Interim_Findings_Memo.pdf [EMAIL-050], prepared by L&L Associates as part of the internal review, reflects counsel's analysis and mental impressions of the review findings. Both work product and attorney-client privilege apply — log under both.

B. Review strategy/budget discussion — work product even without full legal-advice framing

WORKED EXAMPLE

[EMAIL-027] (Ellery discussing a faster review approach, budget, and document-review methodology with Denniston and Marlowe) is opinion work product — it reflects counsel's strategy for conducting the review — in addition to being privileged (see the Attorney-Client Privilege Definition, Rule V.E).

C. IT collection scope — work product prepared at counsel's direction

WORKED EXAMPLE

The IT department's technical export scope (Custodian_Mailbox_Export_List.xlsx, [EMAIL-059]) is fact work product: it was prepared at counsel's direction to define the collection for the internal review and subpoena response, even though it contains no legal advice itself and no attorney is its author.

D. Communications with the IRS are not work product

The extension-request correspondence with IRS Revenue Agent Kevin Tran is not work product — material shared with the investigating government agency (the adverse party) is not protected, the same way any document shared with an adversary loses protection. Analyze such correspondence as an ordinary responsive record, not privileged/work product.

E. Ambiguous business analysis — flag for human review

FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW

Q3_Financial_Impact_Coastal_Solar_Pause.xlsx [EMAIL-071] analyzes the financial effect of pausing the Program. If prepared at counsel's direction as part of a litigation-risk assessment, it is work product; if prepared in the ordinary course of financial reporting, it is not. Absent a clear indication in the document or its transmittal email of counsel's direction, flag for human review rather than presuming either way.

V. Work product and privilege are independent

A document can be work product without being privileged (e.g., the GreenAcre survey and IT export scope above — factual material with no attorney-communication content). A document can be privileged without being work product (e.g., pre-trigger-date legal advice such as [EMAIL-005] or [EMAIL-012], given before the anticipation-of-litigation date). Always assess the two doctrines separately, per the Attorney-Client Privilege Definition, Section VI.

VI. Waiver

Work product protection is waived when the material is disclosed to an adversary or to a third party without a shared interest in maintaining confidentiality — including disclosure to the IRS, or to Alder Point Partners/Bellhaven Advisory personnel, who are not part of CTH's defense team (see the Attorney-Client Privilege Definition, Section IV).

Confidential — Prepared for Legal Review

DECOVERAI · DISCOVERY REFERENCE

Responsiveness definition

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc.

Matter

IRS Examination — Coastal Solar Credit Program

Issued to

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc., Attn: Legal Department, Portland, OR 97209

Issuing agency

Internal Revenue Service, Examination Division

Case no.

EX-2023-04471

Date issued

May 23, 2023

Response due

June 13, 2023 (21 days)

Revenue agent

Kevin Tran

Version

v1.0 — prepared July 16, 2026

I. Purpose

This document defines what makes a record responsive to the IRS summons issued under 26 U.S.C. § 7602 (Case No. EX-2023-04471; called “the subpoena” in the corpus and below) issued to Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc. regarding the Coastal Solar Credit Program. A reviewer (human or LLM) must classify each document as RESPONSIVE or NOT RESPONSIVE and, if responsive, identify which of the five categories below (1–5) it falls under. A document may satisfy more than one category.

The subpoena defines its scope by subject matter — the Program and its surrounding relationships and records — not by custodian, sender, or date alone. A document is responsive because of what it discusses, not who wrote it.

II. Scope categories (subpoena document requests 1–5)

Category 1 — Tax-credit transactions

Records regarding tax-credit transactions involving renewable energy and land conservation programs, including credit origination, eligibility determinations, and transaction structuring documents.

WORKED EXAMPLES

[EMAIL-001] (Program kickoff), [EMAIL-003] (parcel eligibility discrepancy), [EMAIL-004]/[EMAIL-005] (compliance question re: eligibility), [EMAIL-015]/[EMAIL-016] (eligibility follow-up), the underlying Land_Parcel_Data_Northwest.csv [EMAIL-037], and the GreenAcre survey findings [EMAIL-039].

Category 2 — Marketing and sales materials

Marketing and sales materials for the Program, including broker network materials, investor-facing decks, and sales communications distributed in 2022 and 2023.

WORKED EXAMPLES

Coastal_Solar_Marketing_Deck.pptx [EMAIL-001], Alder Point's original pitch deck Coastal_Solar_Partnership_Proposal.pptx [EMAIL-033].

Category 3 — Investor, buyer, seller, land trust, and advisor relationships

Records reflecting relationships with investors, buyers, sellers, land trusts, and advisors in connection with the Program, including engagement letters, correspondence, and agreements.

WORKED EXAMPLES

[EMAIL-002]/[EMAIL-013]/[EMAIL-014]/[EMAIL-026]/[EMAIL-030] (Marlowe–Denniston stakeholder communications about the Program's financial performance and the decision to pause), investor-relations follow-up on the pause.

Category 4 — Alder Point Partners-affiliated entities and brokers

Records concerning corporate entities affiliated with Alder Point Partners, including organizational documents, ownership records, and inter-company agreements, together with any records concerning brokers engaged in connection with the Program, including Bellhaven Advisory.

WORKED EXAMPLES

[EMAIL-006]–[EMAIL-011] (Bellhaven engagement and OR/WA registration gap), [EMAIL-017]/[EMAIL-018] (licensing check-in), [EMAIL-029] (registration finalized), Bellhaven_Coastal_Solar_Placement_Agreement.pdf [EMAIL-009].

Category 5 — Tax, accounting, banking, and loan records

Tax, accounting, banking, and loan records connected to the Program, including general ledger entries, bank statements, loan agreements, and tax filings referencing Coastal Solar credit transactions.

WORKED EXAMPLE

Q3_Financial_Impact_Coastal_Solar_Pause.xlsx [EMAIL-071].

III. Not responsive

A document is NOT responsive if it falls outside all five categories above, regardless of any internal analytical tag it carries in the review platform (e.g., "Routine" or "Chronology Key Event" are workflow labels, not responsiveness determinations — assess against Categories 1–5 directly).

Documents confirmed not responsive in this collection include:

— Calendar invites, out-of-office autoreplies, IT security notices, HR announcements, expense/travel emails, and general unrelated chatter with no connection to the Program.

— Legal-hold and internal-review-process documents that discuss how CTH is responding to the subpoena, rather than the underlying subject matter of Document Requests 1–5 (e.g., [EMAIL-024] legal hold notice, [EMAIL-026]/[EMAIL-027] review budget/approach) — these may be privileged/work product, but they concern the response to the subpoena, not the Program itself. Log separately if privileged; do not mark responsive on that basis alone.

Critical rule — "Mountain Ridge Reforestation Credit" is a false positive

Several documents in this collection concern the "Mountain Ridge Reforestation Credit," a similarly named but entirely separate reforestation program with no connection to Alder Point Partners, Bellhaven Advisory, or the Coastal Solar Credit Program. These are NOT responsive despite superficial keyword overlap ("credit," "reforestation" vs. "conservation"). Do not classify a document as responsive on program-name similarity alone — confirm the actual entities and program at issue.

IV. Privilege is assessed separately

A document can be both responsive and privileged (produced on a privilege log, not in the production set). See the Attorney-Client Privilege Definition and Work Product Definition for that independent analysis. Responsiveness alone does not resolve whether a document must be produced.
